## GitHub: use `ghx` in repos that have `.github/ghx.json`

- In a repo with `.github/ghx.json`, use `ghx` for PRs and CI, not raw `gh`. Elsewhere `ghx` reads still work but aren't required.
- Run `ghx` as one plain command: no pipes, `--jq`, `head`, `sleep` or `timeout`. It bounds its own output and its own time. To keep only some fields, use `--brief` or `--fields a.b,c[].d`, not jq.
- Discover with `ghx --help`, `ghx <cmd> --help` and `ghx <cmd> --schema`. Check setup with `ghx doctor`.
- One call per question:
  - PR state, mergeability, CI for the head SHA and feedback: `ghx pr status <pr>`. Several PRs: `ghx pr status 12 13 14`.
  - All review and comment threads: `ghx pr feedback <pr>`.
  - Why CI failed: `ghx ci why <pr>`, `ghx ci why run:<id>`, or `ghx ci why branch:main` for main.
- Other gh reads (`pr diff`, `pr list`, `issue view`, `run list`, `api` GETs, …) run through ghx: `ghx pr diff 12` returns gh's output in a bounded JSON envelope. `--fields passthrough.json[].<key>` trims it.
- In those repos, writes go through ghx, never raw `gh pr create|edit|merge|comment|review|close|ready` or `gh run rerun`. The ghx verbs check repo policy and pin the head SHA (for `ghx ci rerun run:<id>`, the run).

### JSON input

- Prose (PR bodies, comments, reviews) goes in JSON. Write it to a file with the Write tool, then run `ghx <cmd> --input path.json`.
- Don't build bodies with heredocs, `echo` or `$(…)`.
- `ghx schema <cmd>` lists the fields. Run a write with `--dry-run` first to see exactly what would be sent.

### Waiting for CI

Run `ghx ci wait <pr>` with the Bash tool and `run_in_background: true`. Then continue other work or end your turn. Do not poll, sleep, or use Monitor for CI. You will be re-invoked when it exits. Its stdout is the full answer and its exit code is the outcome.

- A non-zero exit shows as "failed" in the task notification. That label is not the outcome: read the JSON summary (`outcome`, and each result's `diagnosis`, `stalled` and `rerunCandidates`) and the exit code below.
- The target can also be `run:<id>` (say, after a rerun) or `branch:<name>`.
- Don't read the task's output file while it runs, and don't start a second wait on the same PR.
- By default (`--until first-failure`) it returns at the first new failure, so you can start on the fix early. Run the identical command again on the same SHA to continue: it skips the failures it already reported and returns at the next new failure or once CI settles.
- Exit 15 means the wait handed back early in an unattended session. Run the identical command again, in the background; it resumes from cached state.
- With several targets and `--any`, it returns when the first target finishes. Targets still unfinished then show `outcome: "pending"` with `reason: "any-satisfied"`. That is not a hand-back: wait on them again only if you still need them.
- After pushing a fix, wait again. Before merging, `ghx ci wait <pr> --until mergeable` returns the full merge picture in one summary.

### Results and errors

- stdout is one JSON document. Errors are `{"error":{"code","message","hint","details"}}` with a non-zero exit. Follow `hint`; don't retry blindly.
- Big outputs (logs, diffs) come back as file paths. Read the file; don't fetch it again.
- `--brief` (pr status, pr create, pr merge, pr feedback, ci wait, ci why, ci rerun) keeps the fields you'd otherwise extract. Errors are never trimmed.
- With several PRs, `pr status` exits 7 if some `results[]` entries are `error`. Read the document. A slow PR can be a `TIMEOUT` entry while the rest are read; re-run it alone or raise `--timeout`.

### Exit codes

| Exit | Meaning | What to do |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Success. A read that reports red CI still exits 0 | Read the output |
| 1 | ghx bug | Report it |
| 2 | Usage: unknown command or flag, bad input, failed validation | Fix it as the hint says |
| 3 | `.github/ghx.json` missing or invalid | Fix the config |
| 4 | gh missing, too old or not logged in | Ask a human |
| 5 | PR, repo, run or ref not found | Fix the selector or `--repo` |
| 6 | A ghx policy refused the write | Ask the user, or `--override CODE --reason "…"` |
| 7 | gh or API failure after retries, permission, rate limit | Retry later, or fix access |
| 8 | Deadline exceeded | Retry |
| 9 | GitHub state forbids it now: head moved, conflict, CI pending | Change the state, then retry |
| 10 | `ci wait`: CI is red | Read the diagnosis; fix it, or `ghx ci rerun <pr> --flaky` (that also covers jobs that never got a runner, flake `no-runner`). `reason: "workflow-invalid"`: GitHub rejected a workflow file; fix it as `next` says |
| 11 | `ci wait`: red, but every failure so far is also red on main | Under the default first-failure, other checks may still be running: run `ghx ci wait <pr> --until mergeable` before merging |
| 12 | `ci wait`: the head moved, or the PR closed or merged | Re-read with `ghx pr status` |
| 13 | `ci wait`: no checks registered | If `reason` is `merge-conflict`, merge the base and push. Otherwise check the triggers, or `ghx ci retrigger <pr>` |
| 14 | `ci wait`: a check stalled | Read `stalled`; `ghx ci rerun`, or wait again |
| 15 | `ci wait`: handed back while unattended; state is cached (or, under `--any`, `reason: "any-satisfied"`: another target finished first) | Re-run the identical command in the background |
| 130, 143 | Interrupted | Re-run if still needed |

### Commands

- `ghx ci rerun` (write): Rerun failed jobs of completed runs on the PR head, or of one run (--flaky: only likely-flaky jobs)
- `ghx ci retrigger` (write): Fire fresh pull_request workflows by closing and reopening the PR (never left closed)
- `ghx ci wait` (read): Wait for CI on a PR, branch or run; one JSON summary, exit code = outcome (run in background)
- `ghx ci why` (read): Why CI is red: failing jobs, step, tests, errors, log path, shared-with-main and flake
- `ghx doctor` (read): Check the setup: gh version and features, auth, git, the target repo and its config.
- `ghx hook claude-pretooluse` (read): Claude Code PreToolUse hook: background ghx ci wait, steer raw gh to ghx (stdin protocol)
- `ghx init` (write): Write a starter .github/ghx.json (components inferred from the workspace).
- `ghx install` (write): Install the Claude Code hook and CLAUDE.md block, plus deny rules at project scope (try --dry-run).
- `ghx pr comment` (write): Post a typed coordination comment: note, merge precondition, status or supersede
- `ghx pr create` (write): Open a PR from validated JSON: compact body, hidden ghx block, exact read-back
- `ghx pr edit` (write): Patch a ghx PR: re-validated, block rev+1, retarget or draft toggle, exact read-back
- `ghx pr feedback` (read): All PR feedback (reviews, findings, comments, bots), filterable; full bodies in a file
- `ghx pr land` (write): Wait until mergeable, then merge pinned to that head (run like ci wait)
- `ghx pr merge` (write): Merge when policy allows, pinned to the evaluated head; every blocker reported together
- `ghx pr ready` (write): Mark a PR ready for review, or back to draft with --undo; any PR, no ghx block needed
- `ghx pr resolve` (write): Set the status of findings or preconditions (append-only event; resolves the review thread)
- `ghx pr review` (write): Post a review: verdict, inline findings in the diff, hidden blocks, pinned to the head
- `ghx pr status` (read): One object: description, block, merge readiness, CI for the head, feedback, preconditions, stack
- `ghx uninstall` (write): Remove what ghx install added to Claude Code settings and CLAUDE.md (try --dry-run).
- `ghx version` (read): Print the ghx version, Node version and platform (no gh calls).

Full reference: `ghx <cmd> --help`, or docs/agents/commands.md in the ghx repo.
